title: Two concurrent runs of the same workflow -> disjoint workspaces, no shared-path write before publish
rule: specs/aip-58.mdx section 4 Run workspace -- "Two runs MUST NEVER share a workspace" + the deferred-publish model
note_on_manifest: outputsFiles.brief.path is deliberately a FIXED path with no <runId>/<isoDate> interpolation -- './briefs/latest.md' -- the exact shape that raced under plain AIP-16. This is the case the deferred-publish model exists for; V5 under interpolated paths would not exercise the bug at all.

notes: At no point while either run is 'running' does the file at the shared workspace path './briefs/latest.md' get created, truncated, or modified by either run -- outputsFiles.brief syncs ONLY to each run's own <runsRoot>/<runId>/artifacts/brief per section 4's sync-target override.

Reading './briefs/latest.md' at any timestamp strictly between both runs' startedAt and both runs' endedAt MUST show either its pre-existing content or absence -- never partial or run-attributable content from run_A or run_B.

artifactsAfterBothSucceed.invariant: run_A.artifacts[0]'s absolute location (<runsRoot>/run_A/artifacts/brief) and run_B.artifacts[0]'s (<runsRoot>/run_B/artifacts/brief) are disjoint paths, even though both entries carry the identical relative key/path/stepId -- disjointness is a property of the run-scoped root, not of the ArtifactEntry fields themselves.

afterExplicitPublish.scenario: run.publish { runId: run_B, artifactKey: 'brief' } called after run_B succeeds, no explicit 'to' given
afterExplicitPublish.result: ./briefs/latest.md now holds run_B's brief content; a run.published event appears in run_B's event log naming { artifactKey: 'brief', to: './briefs/latest.md' }
notes: run_A's own artifacts/brief is untouched by run_B's publish -- publish only ever writes to the shared destination, never to another run's workspace.

Had run_A also published to the same default destination (before or after run_B), the shared path reflects whichever publish happened last -- last-publish-wins is an explicit, observable act attributable to a specific run.publish call, never an accidental race between two runs finishing.

This is the exact failure the Motivation cites: two runs overwriting each other's files. Before this vector's extension, a naive reading of AIP-16 alone could still let both runs' outputsFiles.brief sync to './briefs/latest.md' unconditionally at run end, racing on whichever finished last -- the deferred-publish model (section 4) is what actually closes it, not merely giving each run its own <runId>.
